small_guidance:
- The current GEMM-K loop iterates `KH*KW*ceil(IC/BLOCK_K)` times with a tiny `IC=64`; collapse the inner channel loop by setting `BLOCK_K=64` (one iteration covers all IC) and keep the `(kh,kw)` static_range outside — this removes loop overhead and lets the compiler keep weight tiles in registers across the 9 spatial taps.
- Add larger configs now that IC fits in one K-step: e.g. `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=2` and `BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=2`; verify SMEM: `(128*64+64*64)*4*2 ≈ 96KB` fits. Drop the currently-useless `BLOCK_K=16/32` variants.
- The N tile indexes `OH*OW=15876` flat — switch to 2D spatial tiling (BLOCK_OH×BLOCK_OW, e.g. 8×32) so `ih=oh+kh, iw=ow+kw` give contiguous-row reuse of x across kw, allowing the inner kw loop to advance by `stride_xw` instead of regathering — this halves global-load traffic on x.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM with the reduction axis ordered as `K = IC * KH * KW` (single flat loop) instead of nested `kh,kw,ic`. Use channels-last input and weight laid out as `[OC, KH*KW*IC]` (already contiguous after permute) so weight loads are pure contiguous GEMM-K reads and `tl.dot` runs on a true `[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K] x [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]` tile without per-iteration index recompute.
- Use 2D output-spatial tiling `(BLOCK_OH, BLOCK_OW)` mapped to one program, with input rows loaded once per `kh` and reused across all `kw` via register-shift (since stride-1 conv: `iw = ow + kw` shares data). Persist OC tile in registers across the whole (OH,OW) tile, fuse `+conv_b, relu, +bias` in epilogue (already done), and write out in NCHW with a transpose store.
- Consider a persistent-CTA design: launch `num_SM * k` programs, each iterating over a queue of `(n, oc_tile, spatial_tile)` work items so launch overhead and L2 reuse of weights across the batch axis improve — at N=128 batches sharing the same 73KB weight tensor, weight reuse via L2 is the dominant win.
